source: Garage limit advisor (out/racing_game_queue.md 'Owner decision: allow extreme turbo setups, show warnings'). Every number the advice shows comes from physics_sim's dyno sweep (ps/drivetrain/engine_dyno.h) and its limit findings; THIS file only decides how findings are merged, what the text says and which kinds the game itself hides. WHICH severities are worth telling, and every threshold physics grades a finding by, are physics_sim's limit policy (physics_sim.limit_policy/1): the file named by limit_policy below, plus an optional user layer <user dir>/limit_policy.json. A kind without min_severity is shown at whatever severity the policy warns about; min_severity (a floor above the policy's) and "never" (hide the kind) are the only game-side filters and appear only where the game genuinely adds one. Nothing here limits a setup value: the garage never clamps, it only advises.
limit_policy_help: The physics_sim limit policy (physics_sim.limit_policy/1) that decides which findings are told (warn_at), which a garage would refuse (refuse_at) and every grading threshold. Relative to this file. data/garage/limit_policy.json extends physics' default; the player's <user dir>/limit_policy.json is merged last.
debounce_ms_help: A setup change must stay unchanged this long before the engine maps and the sweep are started again (a slider drag restarts the wait).

sweep.quality_help: Engine-map quality used for the advisor: sketch (about 0.7 s cold on the hyper V8, then cached), preview or full. Maps of one quality are cached under the game's engine-map cache directory.
sweep.limiter_margin_help: The last swept point lies this far under the rev limit: at the limiter itself every engine reports its own limiter.

merge_gap_help: Findings of one kind closer than this (rpm) belong to one range; keep it a little above rpm_step.

remedy.solve_points_help: A Find fix button runs the wastegate search at these rpm of an item: the worst finding and/or the last (highest-rpm) one; the answer is the larger need.

part_limits.source: [AS] Damage-model data, warnings only. Mean piston speed: production engines run up to about 20-25 m/s at their limiter (sports engines ~24, F1 ~25+); above 25 m/s rods and bearings are the limit. max_mean_piston_speed_m_s is only the fallback for an engine without internals data: with data/engines/engine_internals.json the weakest installed part sets the limit. A part reported Near from 90 % of its rating. The charge piping and turbo ratings come with the parts in data/engines/turbo_kits.json.

TurboStageMapCoverage.option_help: Severity comes from physics_sim (check_turbo_stage_coverage, graded by the limit policy): Near = the target lies partly outside the map's certified cells, Limiting (variant beyond_map) = it needs a rotor speed above the map. {coverage} is the share of the engine's maximum air flow the map covers at the target boost.
TurboStageMapCoverage.title: Turbo map covers only part of the flow
lines: The turbo map covers {coverage} of the engine's air flow.
Beyond that the compressor runs on estimated data.
TurboStageMapCoverage.suggestion: A lower boost target or a turbo with a wider map.

beyond_map.title: Boost target is beyond the turbo map
lines: The turbo map reaches it for {coverage} of the engine's air flow.
Beyond that the turbo is extrapolated.
beyond_map.suggestion: A lower boost target or a larger turbo.

choke.title: Compressor chokes at this boost
lines: Each compressor passes at most {choke_flow} at this boost; the engine wants {demand_flow}.
Above that flow the boost sags. The turbo map itself was extended to cover the rest.
choke.suggestion: A lower boost target or a larger turbo.
choke.max_severity_help: Owner decision 2026-10-14: the compressor's own choke is accepted, not a map problem; never louder than advice.

ChargePipingPressure.option_help: Damage-model data (docs/garage_ui.md "Damage model data"): the boost (the larger of the target and the sweep's charge pressure) against the fitted charge piping's rating (data/engines/turbo_kits.json piping). Near = at near_fraction of the rating, Limiting = above it, Exceeded (variant burst) = at the burst figure. Nothing fails in the simulation yet; the setup still saves.
ChargePipingPressure.title: Boost is above the charge piping's rating
lines: Boost reaches {value}; the {part} is rated for {limit}.
Couplers can blow off and pipes crack above the rating (not simulated yet).
ChargePipingPressure.suggestion: Aluminium or steel charge piping, or a lower boost target.

near.title: Boost is close to the charge piping's rating
lines: Boost reaches {value}; the {part} is rated for {limit}.
near.suggestion: Stronger charge piping before raising the boost further.

burst.title: Boost would burst the charge piping
lines: Boost reaches {value}; the {part} is rated for {limit} and lets go near {burst}.
A real car would lose its boost here (not simulated yet).
burst.suggestion: Steel charge piping, or a much lower boost target.

TurboShaftSpeed.option_help: Damage-model data: the dyno sweep's rotor speed against the kit turbo's rated maximum (scaled reference speed x limits.max_shaft_speed_factor in turbo_kits.json). Garage turbo kits only.
TurboShaftSpeed.title: Turbo overspeeds
lines: The turbo spins at {value} at {rpm}; its rated maximum is {limit}.
An overspeeding wheel can burst (not simulated yet).
TurboShaftSpeed.suggestion: A lower boost target, or more turbos sharing the air.

near.title: Turbo runs close to its speed limit
lines: The turbo spins at {value} at {rpm}; its rated maximum is {limit}.

MeanPistonSpeed.option_help: Damage-model data: mean piston speed 2 x stroke x rpm at the top of the sweep against the WEAKEST installed engine part (connecting rods, pistons, crankshaft; data/engines/engine_internals.json, rg/engine_internals.h). The item's option is then the garage option that swaps that part ({part} names it with its grade, {part_kind} the kind, damage_part is the part a damage model would break); the rev limit (this option) is the fallback for an engine without internals data, rated against part_limits.max_mean_piston_speed_m_s. Any simulated engine. While the parts are known, physics' own MeanPistonSpeed finding (one table figure) is not shown.
MeanPistonSpeed.title: Mean piston speed is very high
lines: At {rpm} the pistons average {value}; the {part} hold {limit} (about {limit_rpm}).
They would be the first to fail above it (damage is not simulated yet).
MeanPistonSpeed.suggestion: Stronger {part_kind}, or a lower rev limit.

near.title: Mean piston speed is close to the limit
lines: At {rpm} the pistons average {value}; the {part} hold {limit} (about {limit_rpm}).

CylinderWall.option_help: Damage-model data: a bored block (data/engines/engine_internals.json "bore") leaves a thinner wall between two cylinders, bore spacing (pitch_factor x factory bore, [AS]) minus the new bore. Below safe_wall_mm the wall flexes and the bores go out of round under load; the item names the cylinder block (damage_part cylinder_block). A geometry figure, not a sweep value: shown at any rpm. Nothing fails yet.
CylinderWall.title: Thin cylinder walls
lines: The {part} leaves {value} of wall between two cylinders; about {limit} is safe.
The bores can go out of round under load (damage is not simulated yet).

ValveFloat.option_help: Damage-model data: the top of the sweep against the rpm the installed valve springs keep the valves on the cam (data/engines/engine_internals.json limit_kind limiter_factor: a factor of the engine's factory limiter). Above it the valves float and can touch the pistons; nothing fails yet.
ValveFloat.title: Valves float at this rev limit
lines: At {value} the valves no longer follow the cam; the {part} hold up to {limit}.
A floating valve can hit a piston (damage is not simulated yet).
ValveFloat.suggestion: Stiffer valve springs, or a lower rev limit.

near.title: Valve springs are close to their limit
lines: At {value} the {part} are close to their limit of {limit}.

loader_warnings.title: Engine data notice
loader_warnings.ignore_containing_help: The stage-map advisory of the engine loader is shown as the build rule above, with its numbers; every other loader warning is passed through as a line.

BoostBelowTarget.title: Excessive turbo boost target
BoostBelowTarget.suggestion: Bigger turbos or a lower boost target.

spool.title: Slow turbo spool-up
spool.max_severity_help: Turbo lag at low rpm is information, not a fault: never louder than advice.

falloff.title: Turbos run out of breath
lines: The turbos hold it up to {drop_rpm}.
falloff.suggestion: Bigger turbos or a lower boost target.

BoostAboveTarget.title: Boost overshoots the target
BoostAboveTarget.suggestion: A bigger wastegate holds the target.
BoostAboveTarget.remedy: Wastegate needs about {ratio_min}x the area, {ratio}x to be safe.
BoostAboveTarget.remedy_failed: Even 8x the wastegate area does not hold it. Try a lower boost target.

WastegateSaturated.title: Wastegate is maxed out
lines: and has no room left to hold it.
WastegateSaturated.suggestion: A bigger wastegate or a lower boost target.
WastegateSaturated.remedy: Wastegate needs about {ratio_min}x the area, {ratio}x to be safe.
WastegateSaturated.remedy_failed: Even 8x the wastegate area does not hold it. Try a lower boost target.

TurboRotorCap.title: Turbos spin too fast
TurboRotorCap.suggestion: A lower boost target or bigger turbos.
TurboRotorCap.remedy: A bigger wastegate fixes it: about {ratio_min}x the area, {ratio}x to be safe.
TurboRotorCap.remedy_failed: A bigger wastegate does not fix it. It needs bigger turbos or a lower boost target.

CompressorChoke.title: Compressor flow is maxed out
CompressorChoke.suggestion: Bigger turbos or a lower boost target.

CompressorSurge.title: Compressor surge
CompressorSurge.suggestion: A smaller compressor or a lower boost target.

RevLimiter.min_severity_help: Hidden: the sweep ends just under the limiter, so this only restates the rev limit setting.
RevLimiter.title: Rev limiter reached
lines: The engine runs into its {limit} limiter @ {rpm}.

FuelCut.min_severity_help: Hidden: the sweep ends just under the limiter, so this only restates the rev limit setting.
FuelCut.title: Rev limiter reached
lines: The engine runs into its {limit} limiter @ {rpm}.

MeanPistonSpeed.title: Pistons move very fast
MeanPistonSpeed.suggestion: A lower rev limit keeps the engine alive.

MapGridEdge.min_severity_help: Near the edge of the engine's data is a modelling detail, not advice; only a clamped lookup (the result is an estimate) is shown.
MapGridEdge.title: Beyond the engine's data range
lines: The engine data only goes up to {limit_kpa}.

rpm.title: Beyond the engine's data range
lines: The engine data only goes up to {limit}.

ClutchCapacity.title: The clutch will slip
ClutchCapacity.remedy: A clutch rated for about {required} holds it with margin (now {current}).

GearboxInputTorque.title: Gearbox overloaded
GearboxInputTorque.remedy: A gearbox rated for about {required} holds it with margin (now {current}).

Knock.title: The engine is knocking
Knock.suggestion: Higher octane fuel or a lower boost target.

KitFuelLean.title: N2O mixture too lean
lines: The mixture under the shot is lambda {value} @ {rpm}.
KitFuelLean.remedy: A kit fuel jet of about {required} (now {current}) runs rich enough.

N2OBottleDuration.title: N2O bottle empties too fast
lines: The bottle lasts {value} at full flow @ {rpm}.
N2OBottleDuration.remedy: A bottle with about {required} of N2O (now {current}) lasts long enough.

N2OBottlePressureDrop.title: N2O flow fades during the shot
lines: By the end of a pass the flow drops to {value_pct}
N2OBottlePressureDrop.suggestion: A heated bottle holds its pressure.
